name: Sterlite Technologies Ltd
title: Sterlite Technologies Ltd - 532374 - Transcript Of Analyst/ Investor Meet Held On September 3, 2026.

read.thesis: Management call on Open RAN and 5G strategy with no company financials; no supply, pricing, or guidance evidence, and prior FY27 guidance (30% enterprise/DC share, 20% EBITDA margin, net debt below 1.2x) is not revisited.

prior_guidance_check.metric: Enterprise and data centre share of revenue

evasions.quote: Not aware of the challenges, but know that they are in the process of transitioning to 5G

summary.headline: STL's Head of Access Solutions outlines Open RAN thesis; no Q1 FY27 financials, guidance or order numbers disclosed in this call.
summary.overview: This is an investor-conference discussion with STL's Head of Access Solutions, not a quarterly results call, so no Q1 FY27 financial figures were presented. The discussion centred on Open RAN, virtualisation and disaggregation, and why operators such as Rakuten and Dish are adopting them. Management described STL's move into fixed-access (FTTX) virtualisation and wireless radio programmes, including a recently announced 5G radio ecosystem for dual and multiband radios. Management also gave a view on Indian 5G timing, fibre backhaul penetration and deployment architecture.

segments.name: Access Solutions (fixed and wireless)
segments.commentary: STL is virtualising FTTX last-mile access and using white-box hardware, with the company saying it is getting close to commercial. On the wireless side it has programmes for radio unit development, a 5G dual and multiband radio ecosystem announced the previous week, and small-cell radios for enterprise indoor and outdoor use.

guidance_outlook: No numerical guidance was given on revenue, margins, order inflows or capex.
Management expects Open RAN to become a norm, with operators moving toward virtualised or disaggregated deployment in at least some 5G segments within about 5 years.
Management is optimistic that adoption accelerates over the next year or two, citing RFIs and RFPs from operators.
capex_capacity: STL has built a RAN intelligent controller software product, which management said manages radio resources based on latency of 10ms or less.
STL has been on an SDN/NFV transformation journey for about two years on the fixed side and about one to one and a half years on the wireless side.
No capacity, utilisation, plant or capex figures were disclosed.
demand_pricing: Management says STL has relationships with tier 1 and tier 2 operators in over 100 countries and 160 operators, built over 25-30 years.
Management cited public estimates of about 40% capex and 30% opex savings from Open RAN (Rakuten), but said actual savings will vary by operator.
Management cited about 25-30% of Indian towers being fibre-connected, with the rest on microwave backhaul.
No pricing, realisation or order-book data was disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why are new-age telcos such as Rakuten and Dish choosing Open RAN over traditional vendors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the traditional model tied operators to single-vendor end-to-end stacks, while disaggregation and virtualisation let operators mix vendors and lower cost per customer and per byte. It also said the approach avoids heavy upfront investment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the practical timeline for operators to adopt Open RAN?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the journey has already begun, citing Rakuten, Dish, Vodafone rural deployments in Africa, Airtel with Altiostar and Vodafone Idea with Mavenir. It called 2021 the breakout year and said it is optimistic over the next year or two.

qa_highlights.question: What does Open RAN mean for India's 5G rollout and vendor mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a mix, with traditional vendors in dense urban areas and Open RAN in tier 2/3 cities. It said spectrum auctions may occur early next year and that operators are in conversations with STL, with no commercial Open RAN deployment in India yet.

qa_highlights.question: How far is India from fibre backhaul needed for 5G?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only about 25-30% of towers are fibre-connected, with microwave backhaul working up to about 200 Mbps and up to about 1 Gbps with extra investment. It said fibre is a necessity for real-time applications and will roll out gradually.

qa_highlights.question: Could India see a standalone (SA) 5G rollout?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said initial rollouts will most likely be non-standalone, with SA deployed over 3-4 years mainly for enterprise use cases needing low latency and SLAs.

risks_watch: Open RAN adoption timing depends on operators; incumbent operators are slow to commit and are only piloting in rural, new or enterprise segments.
Indian spectrum auction timing is not fixed; management cited talk of early next year.
Reliance Jio is building in-house virtualisation capability and has a Samsung-based legacy network, which may limit third-party vendor share.
Management did not quantify STL's revenue, order pipeline or timeline for Open RAN commercial revenue; watch for disclosed wins in the next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident and optimistic on the long-term Open RAN thesis, but evasive on STL-specific numbers: no financials, order details or commercial timelines were given. Several answers were long, and the speaker said he did not have some figures to hand, such as operator 5G spend in India.
key_quotes: At STL my role has been to establish that practice, to bring the whole domain of virtualization, disaggregation and also openness, we will get into that a little bit during the conversation.
I think 2021 would be the break out year.
In 5 years, the operators could be seen transforming in one way or another towards a fully virtualized or disaggregated deployment atleast in some segments of 5G deployment.
